main_message: Best way to break a habit is to drop it
not_on_batch_message: You are not in a set of 21 challenges yet, select a level to start a new one!

challenge0.title: Awakening
challenge0.description: Day one is an invitation to begin this challenge on the right foot. It is the first step towards doing things differently, being more present, dreaming, and believing you can achieve your goals. Choose a phrase or word that inspires you and repeat it throughout the day.
challenge0.reflection_prompt: What was the phrase/word you chose?

challenge1.title: Mindful Walking
challenge1.description: Today is an invitation to set goals: knowing where you are going and why. Mindful walking means knowing where you are now and where you want to go. Set at least one specific academic goal for this week. Write it down and place it somewhere visible.
challenge1.reflection_prompt: What academic goal did you set for this week? And where did you place it?

challenge2.title: Plan
challenge2.description: Today, plan your study schedule for the week. Think about the goals you set yesterday and include the tasks you need to do each day.

challenge3.title: Learning to Learn
challenge3.description: Do you know that moment during exam season when you think, ‘I should have started studying earlier’? Today’s challenge is a chance to do something about it. Review the main concepts covered in your classes today. Spend 25 minutes consolidating what you have learned.
challenge3.reflection_prompt: What was the most important concept you reviewed?

challenge4.title: Silence
challenge4.description: Today is an invitation to find some quiet. Choose a place where you can study without distractions and disconnect from everything else. Spend one hour in quiet by setting your phone, tablet, or computer to ‘Do Not Disturb’, or switch it off.

challenge5.title: Daily Page
challenge5.description: Are you keeping up with your reading? Choose an article, chapter, or book related to your course and read at least three pages. Write down your main questions and reflections.
challenge5.reflection_prompt: What was the main question or reflection you noted down?

challenge6.title: Day of Compassion
challenge6.description: Try to be your own best friend today. Imagine a friend feels unmotivated about academic life. What would you do to help them? Apply that same approach to yourself.
challenge6.reflection_prompt: What act of compassion did you apply to yourself today?

challenge7.title: Weekly Compass
challenge7.description: Congratulations, you have reached the end of your first week. Take some time to reflect. Identify the most important tasks for next week and keep the list somewhere easy to find. Consider what is most important and urgent.
challenge7.reflection_prompt: What is the most important task you identified for next week?

challenge8.title: Question
challenge8.description: Today is an invitation to ask questions. What have you studied or read so far that left you unsure? Ask a teacher or classmate about one of your questions. Seek clarification and deepen your understanding.
challenge8.reflection_prompt: What question did you clarify with a teacher or colleague today?

challenge9.title: Explore
challenge9.description: Do you know or use an app that helps you manage your studies? If so, spend 20 minutes today finding out what works well and what you could improve. If not, talk to a friend or classmate and find out what they use. Explore the options and get to know what is available!
challenge9.reflection_prompt: What study app did you explore or what tip did you receive from a colleague?

challenge10.title: Organise
challenge10.description: Today is an invitation to get organised. Organise your study materials and notes, and remember to keep your study space tidy and functional.

challenge11.title: Day of Being
challenge11.description: Today’s challenge is an invitation to let go of expectations. Take care of yourself by setting aside two hours for leisure and rest. What would you like to do for yourself mindfully today? Simply doing nothing does not count...
challenge11.reflection_prompt: What leisure activity did you choose for yourself today?

challenge12.title: Help
challenge12.description: Are you especially interested in a subject, or do you feel confident in it? Offer to help a classmate. Share what you know and strengthen your collaboration and connection with others. You may find that explaining it also helps you organise your own knowledge.
challenge12.reflection_prompt: Who did you offer to help, and with which subject?

challenge13.title: Knowing When to Pause
challenge13.description: Do you usually take breaks while studying? That is today’s challenge. Whatever happens during your study session, spend 10 minutes on self-care. Go for a walk outdoors, meditate, or take a relaxing break: choose whatever helps you feel better.
challenge13.reflection_prompt: What self-care break did you take while studying?

challenge14.title: Reflect
challenge14.description: Today is an invitation to reflect on a recent academic mistake and how you can improve. Learn from it and adjust your strategies. If it helps, list the mistakes you have noticed and suggest at least one strategy for each.
challenge14.reflection_prompt: What academic mistake did you reflect on, and what improvement did you identify?

challenge15.title: Group Study
challenge15.description: Today is about collaboration. Arrange a study session with a few classmates and choose a topic you all need to review or discuss. Make the most of your different knowledge and study strategies to enrich your learning.
challenge15.reflection_prompt: What was the main topic you studied together today?

challenge16.title: Experiment
challenge16.description: Today is an invitation to try something new. Choose a study technique you have not used before: flashcards, mind maps, the PLEMA method, Feynman technique... There is a whole world to explore. Find out what works best for you!
challenge16.reflection_prompt: What new study technique did you try?

challenge17.title: A Day of Recognition
challenge17.description: Today is a day to appreciate how far you have come. Think about your academic journey and name one positive aspect of it. Recognise your achievements and value your effort. What are you proud of in your journey so far?
challenge17.reflection_prompt: What achievement or positive aspect of your journey did you remember today?

challenge18.title: Putting Knowledge into Practice
challenge18.description: Today’s challenge is to practise. You have read and studied a lot over the past few days. Try a practical exercise or solve a difficult problem related to one of your courses. Show yourself what you can do!

challenge19.title: Face Your Fear
challenge19.description: Big challenges can bring big learning and change. Today is an invitation to face an academic challenge you have been avoiding. Spend 15 minutes tackling something difficult. Do not worry about being perfect; what matters is getting started. You can do this!
challenge19.reflection_prompt: What academic challenge you had been avoiding did you face today?

challenge20.title: Victory Day
challenge20.description: You believed in yourself throughout these 21 days and made things happen. Now reflect on your journey, celebrate your achievements, and set new goals. What will you take away from this challenge? Write one word that describes the experience and choose three actions you will put into practice from now on.
challenge20.reflection_prompt: What word did you choose to describe this experience?

challenge0.title: Horizon
challenge0.description: Welcome to your first challenge! Today, set a specific academic goal for the week. What do you really want to achieve? Remember, it can be something small; what matters is that it is meaningful to you!
challenge0.reflection_prompt: What academic goal did you set for this week?

challenge1.title: Plan
challenge1.description: Today’s challenge is to plan your week. Think about the goal you set yesterday and break it into daily objectives so you know which tasks to do each day. This will help you track your progress and adjust your strategies. Every objective you complete brings you one step closer to what you want to achieve!

challenge2.title: Prioritise
challenge2.description: Sometimes it can be tempting to do several things at once. Today’s challenge is to prioritise: focus on the most important task of the day and finish it before moving on to other activities. Before choosing, check whether there is an important task you have been avoiding. Prioritising gives the most important work the attention it deserves.
challenge2.reflection_prompt: What was the most important task you completed today?

challenge3.title: More Than Reviewing
challenge3.description: Today’s challenge is a chance to catch up with your studies. Review the concepts covered in your classes and spend 90 minutes consolidating what you have learned. For each topic or source you study, prepare a study sheet or summary. Reviewing is a great way to build deep, lasting learning.
challenge3.reflection_prompt: What topic did you turn into a study sheet or summary?

challenge4.title: Silence
challenge4.description: Today is an invitation to find some quiet. Choose a place where you can study without distractions and disconnect from everything else. Decide how long you will study and silence the world around you during that time by setting your phone, tablet, or computer to ‘Do Not Disturb’, or switching it off. Remember to take breaks!

challenge5.title: Critical Analysis
challenge5.description: Are you keeping up with your reading? Choose an article or chapter related to your course and write a critical analysis of it. Consider its strengths and weaknesses, as well as your own interpretation. This is a chance to practise critical thinking and deepen your knowledge. Do not be afraid to express your perspective!
challenge5.reflection_prompt: What strength or weakness did you identify in your critical analysis?

challenge6.title: Journal
challenge6.description: Remember the questions that came up in yesterday’s critical analysis? Today is an invitation to write them down. Reflecting and recording your ideas is an important part of growing as a student. Try noting your questions and insights in a study journal. It can help organise your thinking. Do not worry if the answers do not come straight away; what matters is that you keep learning each day!
challenge6.reflection_prompt: What important question or insight did you record in your study journal?

challenge7.title: Celebrate
challenge7.description: At the end of your first week, take a moment to recognise your effort. Reflect on your progress towards your weekly goals and reward yourself in a healthy way, even if you are not completely satisfied. Celebrating small steps can help maintain motivation and recognise your value. Choose something simple, such as some leisure time, an activity you enjoy, or a small gift for yourself. Keep going; you are doing great work!
challenge7.reflection_prompt: How did you choose to reward yourself for your effort this week?

challenge8.title: Fresh Start
challenge8.description: Start the week on the right foot by organising the study sheets or summaries you made for last week’s classes. An organised study routine can bring a sense of control and confidence. You will see, it is not so difficult...

challenge9.title: Connection
challenge9.description: Today’s challenge is to take care of yourself. Set aside at least 30 minutes for a walk outdoors, preferably somewhere green. Give yourself a break from worries and responsibilities. Connect with nature and take in the views, sounds, and scents. Enjoy every minute without feeling guilty. Self-care is essential for maintaining motivation and focus.

challenge10.title: Overcome
challenge10.description: Do you know that assignment or exercise you have been putting off? Today, give it some time. Face your fears and spend at least an hour working on something you have been avoiding. Do not worry about being perfect; what matters is getting started.
challenge10.reflection_prompt: What assignment or exercise you had been avoiding did you work on today?

challenge11.title: Practice
challenge11.description: Today’s challenge is to improve your communication skills. Do you have a presentation, seminar, or conference coming up? Spend some time practising it. You may feel more confident when speaking in front of an audience!
challenge11.reflection_prompt: What presentation did you practise today?

challenge12.title: Mentorship
challenge12.description: Today’s challenge is to let someone help you. If you need guidance with your studies, look for a mentor. You could attend a teacher’s office hours, ask a more experienced classmate, or talk to someone outside your faculty. If your faculty has a mentoring programme, you could look for help there too. Otherwise, get creative in your search!
challenge12.reflection_prompt: Which teacher, classmate, or mentor did you ask for guidance?

challenge13.title: Question of the Day
challenge13.description: Today is an invitation to follow your curiosity. Think of a relevant question about what you have studied this week and spend some time finding the answer. You can research it yourself or ask a teacher or classmate.
challenge13.reflection_prompt: What question did you ask, and what answer did you find?

challenge14.title: Timed
challenge14.description: Do you know how long it takes you to read an article or solve an exercise? Today’s challenge is to become more aware of how you use your time. Choose a task you need to complete and start a timer. While you work, keep track of your progress. Afterwards, reflect on how it went: ‘Does this amount of time make sense?’, ‘What did I manage to finish?’, ‘Could I do it in less time?’

challenge15.title: Map the Future
challenge15.description: Today’s challenge is to map out what you know. Choose a past exam or a list of exercises and spend some time reviewing it. Try the questions on topics you have studied without looking at your notes, then record the ones you got wrong or found challenging so you can assess your understanding. If you find topics you have not covered yet, do not ignore them: use those questions to preview what you will study and become familiar with the assessment format. This can make exams feel less daunting.
challenge15.reflection_prompt: What was the most challenging question you noted from the exam you reviewed?

challenge16.title: Grow and Learn
challenge16.description: Today’s challenge is to improve. Think of a skill you would like to develop. It could be related to studying, such as writing or research, or something personal, such as time management or communication. Make a plan to develop it. Consider the resources available to you: a course, a book, or help from a classmate. They all count!
challenge16.reflection_prompt: Which skill did you choose to develop, and what is the first step in your plan?

challenge17.title: Embrace Knowledge
challenge17.description: Today’s challenge is to choose a workshop, talk, or webinar about a topic that complements, but is not part of, your course’s core curriculum. It can broaden your knowledge and help you see your field from a wider perspective. Taking part can enrich your skills, show initiative, and help distinguish your professional profile.
challenge17.reflection_prompt: Which workshop, talk, or webinar did you attend?

challenge18.title: Known and Unknown
challenge18.description: Today’s challenge is to practise by imagining you are a teacher for one of your courses. Create an exam based on your review of the material. Prepare for the unknown by thinking about likely topics and question types. This can help identify areas that need more review and prepare you for real assessments. Remember to set aside some time this week to try the exam you created!
challenge18.reflection_prompt: What was the most interesting question type you included in your practice exam?

challenge19.title: Ritual
challenge19.description: Today’s challenge is to establish a bedtime routine. Avoid using electronic devices for at least one hour before bed. Instead, create a ritual that might include light reading, meditation, a warm bath, or listening to music. You may notice your sleep improving. Before putting your phone away, remember to turn on ‘Do Not Disturb’.
challenge19.reflection_prompt: What relaxing activity did you include in your new bedtime ritual?

challenge20.title: The Letter
challenge20.description: You believed in yourself throughout these 21 days and made things happen. Now reflect on your journey, celebrate your achievements, and set new goals. What will you take away from this challenge? Write a letter to your future self about the kind of student you would like to be, your goals and ambitions, and how you plan to reach them. Make a commitment to yourself and keep the letter somewhere convenient. A note on your phone counts!
challenge20.reflection_prompt: What was the main commitment you made to yourself in your letter?
